priors.applicability: Prefer while the drawer is open and stable, fingers are closed, the object is outside/above the tunnel, and two causal frames show object and TCP moving together; especially when object entry pose is displaced from the demonstrated approximately x=-0.630..-0.619, y=-0.401..-0.388, z=0.285..0.314 range. It may remain active through descent and opening, but should yield after the object has settled because the object is no longer the correct reference for the fixed handle.

handoff.entry_conditions: Drawer open and stable; fingers closed; block outside and above the tunnel; two causal frames indicate block and TCP translate together; current posture is plausibly reachable.
handoff.exit_conditions: Block is at drawer-floor height inside the cavity, no longer follows TCP after opening, TCP has begun collision-free upward retreat, or selection transfers earlier in the shared release region.
handoff.failure_signatures: Object ceases to follow TCP before the cavity, object/TCP relative transform changes abruptly while closed, object pose is unreliable, object settles outside the cavity, or post-release handle motion shifts with an off-center object.
handoff.overlap_role: Retains all actions 680:1160. Actions 680:840 provide 160 supervised actions shared with retrieval; actions 900:1160 provide 260 supervised actions shared with drawer closing, including lowering/opening, settling, retreat, reorientation and handle approach.
handoff.successor_readiness: The phase-aware or destination-frame place policy can take over during lowering/release; close_drawer may receive in 900:1160 but drawer motion waits until the object is settled and detached. At the late boundary the free gripper is at the handle.

Poses are metres and wxyz in the world observation; both are resolved from each causal observation and again from the fresh execution observation."}
priors.limitations: Object-relative decoding assumes a reliable current block pose and attachment-like motion during transport; it does not prove a grasp. After release, an off-center block would incorrectly shift retreat and handle targets, so the destination-frame policy is the intended cover. Rigid frame equivariance does not guarantee collision-free motion, IK reachability, or recovery from unseen slips/drops. Fresh IK starts from measured joints and may report failure near limits.
priors.pipeline_implications: The high-level agent selects this prior for displaced but plausibly held retrieval handoffs. Once the object reaches drawer-floor height and no longer follows TCP, switch in the 900:1160 supervised overlap to the destination-frame prior for fixture-anchored retreat/handle approach, or to the phase-aware local prior when release state is ambiguous. Do not select it as recovery for a dropped object.
priors.rationale: Observed: at entry the block and TCP are close and move together with a closed command, but entry block pose varies across demonstrations (for example demo12100 index 680 versus demo12102 index 680), then both traverse from the tunnel side toward the drawer (indices 780-840), descend over the cavity (860-900), and separate only after an open command and settling (900-920). Likely deployment failure: a preceding retrieval policy can hand off with the held block outside the narrow demonstrated entry range, causing a world-frame policy to reproduce the memorized route instead of preserving the grasp transform. Mechanism: labels and decoded targets use current object pose as the action frame; inputs include object-canonical TCP and destination geometry plus measured qpos/qvel, preserving arm reachability and posture dependence. Expected, not observed, benefit: equivariance of the Cartesian target to a rigid displacement of the observed block during the attached portion.
priors.statement: Live object-frame SE(3) transport: diffuse each demonstrated commanded TCP target as object-relative translation (m), rotation 6D, and gripper scalar, and reconstruct the world target from the freshly observed block pose at every executed slot. This targets displacement and orientation changes of the held block at the retrieval handoff, by construction, primarily from carry through descent/release.

priors.applicability: Prefer when target_pose is reliable and the drawer is open, particularly near cavity alignment, lowering, opening, release confirmation, retreat, and handle transition, or whenever the destination/drawer is displaced relative to training. It is also the preferred cover after an off-center but valid deposit because its retreat and handle targets do not shift with the settled block.

handoff.entry_conditions: Drawer open/stable; target_pose available; block plausibly held or already over the cavity; measured joints admit a collision-free approach in the demonstrated responsibility.
handoff.exit_conditions: Block rests inside the cavity at drawer-floor height and is detached; TCP retreats above the cavity and reaches the handle approach, ready for close_drawer.
handoff.failure_signatures: Target pose jumps or is unavailable, block does not follow closed TCP before release, descent is outside cavity bounds, object remains suspended after opening, or IK residual/limit diagnostics indicate the shifted fixture target is unreachable.
handoff.overlap_role: Retains every 680:1160 action. The 680:840 retrieval overlap covers the transfer into destination coordinates; the 900:1160 closing overlap covers release confirmation, retreat and fixture-relative handle approach/grasp.
handoff.successor_readiness: close_drawer may take over in the shared 900:1160 region, but must not move the drawer until object z is at floor height and two frames show it stationary relative to the drawer. Late handoff occurs with TCP near the handle and object deposited.

priors.invocation_contract: {"call_args_schema":{"type":"object","additionalProperties":false,"properties":{"destination_pose_field":{"type":"string","enum":["target_pose"]},"manipulated_object_pose_field":{"type":"string","enum":["object_pose"]}},"required":["destination_pose_field","manipulated_object_pose_field"]},"parameter_semantics":"destination_pose_field names the live observed world pose, in metres and wxyz, that defines the Cartesian action frame and is resolved at every causal and execution observation; manipulated_object_pose_field names the live block pose used for destination-relative conditioning and release evidence."}
priors.limitations: The destination frame is assumed to move rigidly with the relevant drawer geometry and to be accurately observed. A large held-block displacement is not removed from the input/action mapping by construction, and the model may choose a memorized approach before it has re-aligned the object. Relative decoding does not ensure cavity clearance, attachment, or IK feasibility. Demonstrations contain no recovery from a premature drop.
priors.pipeline_implications: The high-level agent may enter from retrieval or from the object-frame prior before/over the cavity. It should keep this prior through release and post-release retreat when the destination is displaced. If the held object begins far from demonstrated destination-relative entry support, use the object-frame policy for the transfer; if current release phase is ambiguous or the TCP is locally perturbed, use the phase-aware local policy. close_drawer receives through 900:1160 only after settling.
priors.rationale: Observed: transport converges above target_pose near x=-0.175,y=0 before descent (demo12100 indices 840-900); after opening, the object settles near z=0.063 while TCP holds near z=0.126 (920), rises (940-960), then moves to the handle approach near x=-0.44 (1080-1159). target_pose tracks the drawer coordinate through its world x value. Likely deployment failure: displacement of the drawer or target makes memorized world coordinates miss the cavity or handle corridor. Mechanism: destination-canonical history and destination-relative labels/decoding make all Cartesian targets rigidly follow the observed destination frame while measured qpos/qvel retain reachability/posture information. Expected benefit is destination displacement equivariance, not evidence of unseen-displacement success.
priors.statement: Live destination-frame cavity anchoring: diffuse commanded TCP pose as translation (m), canonical unit quaternion wxyz, and gripper scalar relative to the current target_pose. Decode through the freshly observed destination frame at every slot. This targets displacement of the open drawer/placement goal and keeps lowering, release, retreat, and the fixture-relative transition toward the handle anchored to the drawer rather than to where the block happens to settle.

priors.applicability: Prefer when block and destination are within the demonstrated geometric corridor but current TCP/object height, lag, or release timing differs from a nominal trajectory, and two causal frames provide consistent phase evidence. It is useful in the 900:1160 overlap for deciding whether to hold, open, retreat, or present at the handle. Do not prefer it for a large rigid displacement of the held block or drawer; those are covered by the object- and destination-frame priors.

handoff.entry_conditions: Drawer open/stable; observations and measured joints valid; block plausibly attached for carry entry or visibly in the cavity/release corridor for mid-skill entry; current state is not an unseen drop recovery.
handoff.exit_conditions: Causal geometry indicates object stationary at drawer-floor height and detached, TCP has retreated, and preferably the gripper has reached the handle approach for close_drawer.
handoff.failure_signatures: Auxiliary phase conflicts with observed object/TCP motion, object stops following before release, open command occurs while outside the cavity, object continues to follow after opening, local deltas repeatedly grow/drift, or IK reports nonconvergence/limits.
handoff.overlap_role: All 680:1160 actions are supervised. The 680:840 overlap admits predecessor variation; the large 900:1160 overlap explicitly trains opening, settling holds, retreat, reorientation, handle approach and re-closing.
handoff.successor_readiness: Transfer to close_drawer only when observed object height/motion supports deposited-retreat or handle-ready, not from the auxiliary class alone. Preserve two-frame history across the switch. Late transfer is at the handle.

priors.invocation_contract: {"call_args_schema":{"type":"object","additionalProperties":false,"properties":{"manipulated_object_pose_field":{"type":"string","enum":["object_pose"]},"destination_pose_field":{"type":"string","enum":["target_pose"]},"phase_vocabulary":{"type":"string","enum":["carry_release_retreat_handle"]}},"required":["manipulated_object_pose_field","destination_pose_field","phase_vocabulary"]},"parameter_semantics":"The two pose-field arguments select the live block and drawer-goal observations used to form causal relative geometry in metres and wxyz. phase_vocabulary selects the declared four-class auxiliary semantics: 0 carry/closed descent, 1 opening or settling, 2 deposited retreat, 3 handle-ready/re-closing. It is conditioning guidance, not contact truth."}
priors.limitations: Current-TCP increments can accumulate error and do not make global object/destination displacements invariant. Stage labels are coarse, derived from demonstrated action/geometry, and cannot establish contact; unseen failure recovery is unsupported. Two frames may be insufficient for noisy or occluded settling. Rotation-vector labels can be difficult near pi, though demonstrated per-step relative targets are local. IK and collision feasibility remain required.
priors.pipeline_implications: The high-level agent chooses this local policy at perturbed intermediate states with reliable observations. It can take over from either invariant-frame policy in the fully supervised slice, and transfer to close_drawer after deposited-retreat/handle-ready evidence. If the whole object pose is displaced while attached, select object-frame; if the fixture/goal is displaced, select destination-frame. The auxiliary stage is advisory and is not a contact detector or success predicate.
priors.rationale: Observed: the skill contains distinct but adjacent modes—closed carry/descent (680-900), opening and variable settling timing (demo12100 910-920, demo12102 900-905, demo12104 895-900), open upward retreat (920-960), and handle approach/re-closing (1080-1159). The same spatial neighborhood around the drawer therefore supports different gripper and motion commands. Likely deployment failure: a predecessor or chunk boundary enters at an intermediate state, and a globally parameterized policy confuses descent, settling, or retreat. Mechanism: action labels are one-step targets relative to each pre-action measured TCP, so fresh-state decoding acts as local feedback; two causal frames expose object-following and motion; a four-stage auxiliary classifier regularizes the shared trainable condition latent that directly conditions the unchanged DP backbone. Expected benefit is improved local correction and phase separation, not demonstrated recovery.
priors.statement: Phase-aware local Cartesian corrections: diffuse each commanded target as a current-TCP-frame translation increment (m), rotation vector (rad), and gripper scalar, decoded from the fresh measured TCP at each slot. A registered causal condition encoder also predicts carry, opening/settling, deposited-retreat, or handle-ready stage with a masked auxiliary loss. This targets intermediate-state perturbations and release/retreat phase ambiguity rather than large rigid displacement.
